text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Sharp fall in Kuwait Stock Exchange. Index drops 14 points to 1,905.8.
- Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan says Kuwait is preparing a new law to encourage foreign investments.
- U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry due in Kuwait. Perry starts a tour this week to visit American troops in Bosnia, the Gulf and Japan.
- Government keen on supporting the domestic industrial sector, Prime Minister Sheikh Saad says.
- Kuwait to resume issuing work permits for foreigners in January after a month suspension, labour ministry says.
- Trade and Industry Minister Jassem al-Mudaf discusses trade obstacles with visiting Canadian delegation.
- Finance Minister Rodhan says Kuwait plans to emerge as a regional financial centre.

- Prime Minister Sheikh Saad urges aircraft engineers and pilots to call off strike. Kuwait aviation workers' union plans to delay flights by one hour for four days as of Wednesday to press Kuwait Airways Corp (KAC) to improve wages.
- Kuwait's population crossed the two million mark in June 1996.
- Defence Minister Sheikh Salem denies that Kuwait was pressured to purchase weapons from certain countries.
- Communication Ministry to introduce on Saturday lower rates for pagers and mobile telephones.
